the study of the infrared behaviour of the gluon and ghost propagators in the Landau-gauge Yang–Mills theory in four dimensions.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the gluon propagates with a mass of the order of the confinement scale.
the gluon propagates in a way which is compatible with the existence of a gluon mass of the order of the confinement scale, but not necessarily equal to the string tension.
the gluon propagates with a mass of the order of 1 GeV and with a momentum-dependent damping factor of the form [Λ 2 /(p 2 + Λ 2 )] α.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Landau gauge gluon propagator does not vanish at zero momentum.
the Landau gauge gluon propagator is well described by a massless pole with a non-trivial running coupling.
the gluon propagates as a massless field at large momenta and that it is not propagating at all at small momenta.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the Landau-gauge gluon propagator, the infrared region is not dominated by an infrared singularity, as previously suggested in the literature.
the gluon propagators in Landau gauge is not a constant at large momenta, as previously thought, but rather a decreasing function of p 2.
the gluon propagates as an asymptotically massive particle with mass of the order of the Landau pole.
